assumptions: The enzyme cuts every recognition site it meets, and matching overhangs ligate.
limits: Predicts the products, not their yield or ligation fidelity (score_overhang_fidelity grades that); only the first is emitted.
bio.jane/contract.question: What construct do these parts make in a Type-IIS (Golden Gate, MoClo) reaction?

description: Assemble parts with a Type-IIS enzyme (Golden Gate / MoClo, DnaCauldron). Emits the first construct as a NEW record for downstream nodes.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

connectors.description: candidate bridging LINKERS, a library distinct from `parts`. The engine reaches for one as a FALLBACK, where the parts alone do not close a construct, and names the ones it added in `warnings`; a candidate it does not need is silently unused.

enzyme.description: Type-IIS enzyme, or leave unset to let DnaCauldron pick one.

expect_no_unused_parts.description: treat a part the assembly did not consume as an error, which is DnaCauldron's own default.

expected_constructs.description: expect exactly this many constructs and fail when the count differs. Leave unset to enumerate every valid one.

include_subject.description: also include the node's subject as a part.

parts.description: the parts to assemble — wire upstream `record` outputs here, or list library document names/ids.

name: golden_gate_assemble

errors.description: assembly errors — the structured flaws DnaCauldron's errors spreadsheet is built from

overhangs.description: the first construct’s junction overhangs, in assembly order: wire this into score_overhang_fidelity

record.description: the first assembled construct, as a record
